intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn the present continuous, the English 'sedang' form: how to say what is happening right now, like 'I'm cooking' or 'She's reading'. You'll also learn when to use it and when to use the simple present (I cook, she reads) for habits. Warm-up: what are you doing now?
teachingNotes: Form: am/is/are + verb-ing (I'm cooking, she's reading, they're working). Indonesian marks 'now' with 'sedang' and has no 'be', so the #1 error is dropping am/is/are: *'I cooking now' → 'I'm cooking now'. The second is dropping -ing: *'She is cook'.

-ing spelling: most verbs just add -ing (cook → cooking, play → playing, study → studying); a final -e drops (make → making, write → writing); short verbs ending consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter (run → running, sit → sitting), but never w, x or y (play → playing, fix → fixing). *'runing' and *'makeing' are typical errors.

Explain the spelling jargon plainly: vowels = a, e, i, o, u; consonants = the other letters; a 'short verb' = one beat (run, sit, swim). Show why some words don't double: two vowels before the last letter (cook, read, rain → cooking, reading, raining), two consonants at the end (work, help → working, helping), or two beats (listen → listening).

Contrast: present continuous for now / right now / at the moment / today / Look! / Listen!; simple present for habits and routines (every day, usually, on Mondays). Common error: *'I am go to school every day' → 'I go to school every day'. A good pattern: 'I usually walk to school, but today I'm taking the bus.'

Indonesian often leaves out 'sedang' (Lihat! Hujan turun. / Hari ini saya naik bus), so tell learners to decide by meaning (is it happening now / only today?), not by looking for the word 'sedang'. In 'It's raining', it means nothing: English just needs a word at the start. In 'he's having lunch', have = eat (an action), so -ing is fine. In 'What do you do?', the first do only makes the question, the second means 'work/do'.

Negatives and questions work like 'to be': I'm not working, she isn't sleeping; Are you listening? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. Teach 'What are you doing?' as a set phrase and contrast it with 'What do you do?' (= your job).

Limits: don't teach the future use (I'm meeting him tomorrow), past continuous, -ie → -ying (lie → lying) or stress-based doubling (begin → beginning). If a learner asks about 'I'm liking', just say that like, want and know usually stay in the simple form; don't go deeper.

keyPoints.title: am / is / are + -ing
keyPoints.explanation: Use am/is/are + verb-ing (the action word + -ing) for actions happening now. Never drop am/is/are. Spelling: most verbs add -ing; drop a final -e (make → making); double the last letter of one-beat verbs that end with one vowel + one consonant, like run → running and sit → sitting (but cook → cooking: two vowels).

examples.id: Saya sedang memasak makan malam sekarang.

examples.en: The kids are running in the park.

id.title: am / is / are + -ing
id.explanation: Pakai am/is/are + kata kerja-ing (kata kegiatan + -ing) untuk kegiatan yang sedang terjadi sekarang. Jangan pernah hilangkan am/is/are. Ejaan: kebanyakan kata kerja cukup ditambah -ing; buang -e di akhir (make → making); gandakan huruf terakhir pada kata kerja satu ketukan yang berakhiran satu vokal + satu konsonan, seperti run → running dan sit → sitting (tapi cook → cooking: dua vokal).

keyPoints.title: Now or every day?
keyPoints.explanation: Use the present continuous for what is happening now (now, right now, at the moment, today, Look!). Use the simple present for habits and routines (every day, usually, on Mondays). Decide by meaning, not by the word 'sedang': Indonesian often leaves it out.

examples.en: I usually walk to school, but today I'm taking the bus.
examples.id: Saya biasanya jalan kaki ke sekolah, tapi hari ini saya naik bus.

examples.en: Budi works in a bank. Right now he's having lunch.
examples.id: Budi bekerja di bank. Sekarang dia sedang makan siang.

id.title: Sekarang atau setiap hari?
id.explanation: Pakai present continuous untuk yang sedang terjadi sekarang (now, right now, at the moment, today, Look!). Pakai simple present untuk kebiasaan dan rutinitas (every day, usually, on Mondays). Tentukan dari artinya, bukan dari ada tidaknya kata 'sedang': bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakainya.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Complete with 'play': Look! The children ___ football in the garden.
assessment.rubric: Correct: are playing. 'playing' without are = 30 (missing be). 'is playing' = 60 (wrong be for plural). 'play' or 'are play' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Choose the -ing form of 'stop'.
assessment.rubric: Correct: stopping (short verb, consonant + vowel + consonant → double the p). 'stoping' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Listen. Choose the -ing word you hear.
assessment.listen: Sari is dancing at the party.
assessment.rubric: Correct: dancing (dance drops the final e). 'danceing' = 50. 'dansing' = 40. A different word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Make it negative: Dimas is watching TV.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Dimas isn't watching TV. 'Dimas not watching TV' = 30. 'Dimas doesn't watching TV' = 20. 'Dimas doesn't watch TV' = 30 (changes the tense).

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Complete with 'go': Rina ___ to the office by bus every day.
assessment.rubric: Correct: goes ('every day' = routine → simple present). 'go' = 40 (missing -es). 'is going' or 'is go' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Complete with 'wear': Andi usually wears a T-shirt, but today he ___ a batik shirt.
assessment.rubric: Correct: is wearing ('but today' = now, not the usual habit). 'wears' = 30. 'wearing' without is = 40. 'is wear' = 30.

blocks.text: Use the present continuous (the English 'sedang' form) for actions happening **now**. Form: **am / is / are + verb-ing** (the action word + -ing: *cook → cooking*). In speech we use short forms: **I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're** (the mark **'** shows that letters are left out: I'm = I am). It's like Indonesian **sedang**, but English always needs am/is/are.

id.text: Present continuous (bentuk 'sedang' dalam bahasa Inggris) dipakai untuk kegiatan yang terjadi **sekarang**. Bentuknya: **am / is / are + kata kerja-ing** (kata kegiatan + -ing: *cook → cooking*). Saat bicara kita pakai bentuk pendek: **I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're** (tanda **'** menunjukkan ada huruf yang dihilangkan: I'm = I am). Mirip dengan **sedang** dalam bahasa Indonesia, tapi bahasa Inggris selalu butuh am/is/are.

rows.id: Saya sedang memasak makan malam sekarang.

rows.en: Pak Budi is talking on the phone.
rows.id: Pak Budi sedang berbicara di telepon.
Lihat! Hujan turun. (*it* di sini tidak ada artinya: bahasa Inggris cuma butuh kata di depan)
rows.note: It's raining = sedang hujan; it means nothing here

id.note: It's raining = sedang hujan; it di sini tidak ada artinya

blocks.text: Don't drop am/is/are: say **I'm cooking now**, not 'I cooking now'. And don't drop the -ing: say **She is cooking**, not 'She is cook'. Careful: Indonesian often leaves out *sedang* (*Lihat! Hujan turun.*), but if it's happening now, English still uses am/is/are + -ing.

id.text: Jangan hilangkan am/is/are: ucapkan **I'm cooking now**, bukan 'I cooking now'. Dan jangan hilangkan -ing: ucapkan **She is cooking**, bukan 'She is cook'. Hati-hati: bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakai *sedang* (*Lihat! Hujan turun.*), tapi kalau kegiatannya terjadi sekarang, bahasa Inggris tetap memakai am/is/are + -ing.

blocks.explain: It's happening now, so we need is + -ing: is crying.

id.explain: Ini terjadi sekarang, jadi kita perlu is + -ing: is crying.

blocks.text:
Most verbs just add **-ing**: cook → cooking, play → playing, study → studying. If the verb ends in **-e**, drop the e: make → making, write → writing. Short verbs that end **consonant + vowel + consonant** double the last letter: run → running, sit → sitting, get → getting. (Not w, x or y: play → playing, fix → fixing.)

What do the words mean? **Vowels** are **a, e, i, o, u**; **consonants** are all the other letters. **Short** means one beat when you say it: *run, sit, swim* (not *lis-ten*).

id.text:
Kebanyakan kata kerja cukup ditambah **-ing**: cook → cooking, play → playing, study → studying. Kalau kata kerjanya berakhiran **-e**, buang e-nya: make → making, write → writing. Kata kerja pendek yang berakhiran **konsonan + vokal + konsonan** menggandakan huruf terakhirnya: run → running, sit → sitting, get → getting. (Kecuali w, x atau y: play → playing, fix → fixing.)

Apa artinya? **Vokal** adalah huruf **a, e, i, o, u**; **konsonan** adalah semua huruf lainnya. **Pendek** artinya satu ketukan saat diucapkan: *run, sit, swim* (bukan *lis-ten*).

blocks.explain: Write ends in -e, so drop the e and add -ing: writing. Only one t.

id.explain: Write berakhiran -e, jadi buang e-nya lalu tambah -ing: writing. Huruf t-nya cuma satu.
id.prompt: Lengkapi dengan bentuk -ing dari write: Budi is ___ a letter. (write)

blocks.text:
Beginners often ask: *cook* is short and ends with a consonant, so why not 'coocking'? Because the rule needs **exactly one vowel** before the last letter. Look at the **last three letters** and say the word out loud:
- **one** vowel between two consonants, and **one** beat (r-**u**-n, s-**i**-t) → double: **running, sitting**.
- **two** vowels before the end (c-**oo**-k, r-**ea**-d, r-**ai**-n) → just add -ing.
- **two** consonants at the end (wo-**rk**, he-**lp**) → just add -ing.
- **two** beats (*LIS-ten*, *VI-sit*) → just add -ing.

id.text:
Pemula sering bertanya: *cook* pendek dan berakhiran konsonan, kenapa bukan 'coocking'? Karena aturannya butuh **tepat satu vokal** sebelum huruf terakhir. Lihat **tiga huruf terakhir** dan ucapkan katanya:
- **satu** vokal di antara dua konsonan, dan **satu** ketukan (r-**u**-n, s-**i**-t) → gandakan: **running, sitting**.
- **dua** vokal sebelum akhir (c-**oo**-k, r-**ea**-d, r-**ai**-n) → cukup tambah -ing.
- **dua** konsonan di akhir (wo-**rk**, he-**lp**) → cukup tambah -ing.
- **dua** ketukan (*LIS-ten*, *VI-sit*) → cukup tambah -ing.

rows.id: berenang: s-w-**i**-m, satu vokal → gandakan m

blocks.text: Not sure? Say the word and count the vowels before the last letter. One vowel and one beat → double. Anything else → just add -ing.

id.text: Ragu? Ucapkan katanya dan hitung vokal sebelum huruf terakhir. Satu vokal dan satu ketukan → gandakan. Selain itu → cukup tambah -ing.

blocks.explain: Rain ends a-i-n: two vowels (ai) before the n, so don't double: raining.

id.explain: Rain berakhiran a-i-n: ada dua vokal (ai) sebelum n, jadi tidak digandakan: raining.
id.prompt: Lengkapi dengan bentuk -ing dari rain: Look! It's ___. (rain)

blocks.text: It works like **to be**. Negative: add **not** (I'm not, he isn't, they aren't). Question: put **am/is/are** first. Short answers: **Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.** To ask about now, say **What are you doing?**

id.text: Caranya sama seperti **to be**. Kalimat negatif: tambahkan **not** (I'm not, he isn't, they aren't). Kalimat tanya: taruh **am/is/are** di depan. Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.** Untuk bertanya tentang sekarang, ucapkan **What are you doing?**

rows.id: Ibu tidak sedang tidur. Dia sedang membaca.

rows.en: Are you listening? — Yes, I am.
What are you doing? — I'm studying English.
rows.id: Kamu sedang apa? — Saya sedang belajar bahasa Inggris.

blocks.prompt: ___ Rina working today? — Yes, she is.
blocks.explain: Present continuous questions start with am/is/are. Rina = she → Is.

id.explain: Pertanyaan present continuous diawali am/is/are. Rina = she → Is.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ Rina working today? — Yes, she is.

blocks.text: Use the **present continuous** for now: *now, right now, at the moment, today, Look!, Listen!* Use the **simple present** for habits and routines: *every day, usually, on Mondays*. Compare: *I work in Bandung* (my job) and *I'm working at home today* (only today). Decide by the meaning, not by the word *sedang*: *Hari ini saya naik bus* has no *sedang*, but it's only today, so **I'm taking the bus**.

id.text: Pakai **present continuous** untuk sekarang: *now, right now, at the moment, today, Look!, Listen!* Pakai **simple present** untuk kebiasaan dan rutinitas: *every day, usually, on Mondays*. Bandingkan: *I work in Bandung* (pekerjaanku) dan *I'm working at home today* (hanya hari ini). Tentukan dari artinya, bukan dari kata *sedang*: *Hari ini saya naik bus* tidak memakai *sedang*, tapi hanya hari ini, jadi **I'm taking the bus**.

rows.en: I usually walk to school, but today I'm taking the bus.
rows.id: Saya biasanya jalan kaki ke sekolah, tapi hari ini saya naik bus.

rows.en: Budi works in a bank. Right now he's having lunch.
rows.id: Budi bekerja di bank. Sekarang dia sedang makan siang. (*have lunch* = makan siang, sebuah kegiatan, jadi boleh pakai -ing)

rows.en: What do you do? — I'm a nurse.
rows.id: Apa pekerjaanmu? — Saya perawat. (*do* pertama hanya untuk membuat pertanyaan; *do* kedua = bekerja/melakukan)

id.note: pekerjaan, bukan yang sedang terjadi sekarang

blocks.text: For habits with every day, usually or on Mondays, don't add am/is/are: say **I go to school every day**, not 'I am go to school every day'.

id.text: Untuk kebiasaan dengan every day, usually atau on Mondays, jangan tambahkan am/is/are: ucapkan **I go to school every day**, bukan 'I am go to school every day'.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan ___ the newspaper every morning.
blocks.explain: 'Every morning' is a routine, so use the simple present: reads.

id.explain: 'Every morning' adalah rutinitas, jadi pakai simple present: reads.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan ___ the newspaper every morning.

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar present continuous, bentuk 'sedang' dalam bahasa Inggris: cara mengatakan apa yang sedang terjadi sekarang, seperti 'I'm cooking' atau 'She's reading'. Kamu juga akan belajar kapan memakainya dan kapan memakai simple present (I cook, she reads) untuk kebiasaan. Pemanasan: kamu sedang apa sekarang?

Apa bedanya 'What are you doing?' dan 'What do you do?'
